hypotheses.mechanism: Compare current candidate context with strictly prior purchase contexts from matched covered windows.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: General recency/activity or scarce prior-purchase support explains all effect.
hypotheses.next_gate: Same-count/same-recency worlds, common covered windows, nondegenerate reference times; then separately reserved100Q support/cost.
hypotheses.testable_prediction: Equal candidate counts and recencies can yield unequal context-match scores; a separately reserved purchase-ranking contrast can falsify value beyond those controls.
hypotheses.nearest_experiment: Literal equal-count/equal-recency context worlds plus covered-window and nondegenerate-reference gates; no data scan or fit yet.
hypotheses.benefit_towardTask1: Adds a typed historical-reference operator whose support, discovery cost and contribution can be audited against manual counts.

hypotheses.mechanism: Share most learner weights while independently supervising multiple initialized heads, then aggregate predictions.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Correlated heads add cost; any gain follows parameter/CPU differences.
hypotheses.next_gate: Mean-per-head loss, exact variant/initialization/aggregation and parameter/activation ledger before dependency/resource admission.
hypotheses.testable_prediction: Mean per-head loss differs from loss of the mean; head diversity may help only if it survives matched parameter/CPU and stronger-incumbent controls.
hypotheses.nearest_experiment: Literal loss/aggregation witness and exact variant/head/parameter/dependency ledger before any newly reserved training.
hypotheses.benefit_towardTask1: Checks automation against a stronger affordable learner and guards against improvements caused only by a weak baseline.

hypotheses.mechanism: Screen typed parent pairs for contextual target synergy before grammar expansion rather than pruning every weak marginal parent.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Entropy noise or an interaction already learned by boosting explains apparent gain.
hypotheses.next_gate: Literal XOR/redundancy and66pair-screen accounting; same legal opportunities/closure versus marginal-first.
hypotheses.testable_prediction: A marginally uninformative XOR pair remains useful jointly; pair-first selection should retain that opportunity at the declared total screen cost.
hypotheses.nearest_experiment: Literal XOR/redundancy worlds and an explicit66-screen ledger for12 parents against marginal-first with the same legal universe.
hypotheses.benefit_towardTask1: Tests a concrete automatic search policy that can discover useful interactions while exposing all search work.

hypotheses.mechanism: Compute antisymmetric second-order areas between event-action streams while preserving unordered timestamp peers.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Length, logging repeats or ordinary recencies capture all useful information.
hypotheses.next_gate: Seven-event nonalias, unordered peers, rolling expiry and legal nonidentity shuffle.
hypotheses.testable_prediction: Two histories with identical counts and last-event times can have distinct action-path areas; legal nonidentity shuffle should remove the order contrast.
hypotheses.nearest_experiment: Seven-event nonalias witness, peer/rolling-expiry boundary cases and legal shuffle closure before any real-data pilot.
hypotheses.benefit_towardTask1: Adds an interpretable typed temporal-order family beyond manual count/recency operators, with explicit state and scan costs.

hypotheses.mechanism: Retrieve strictly mature other-user prefix situations and their later purchase continuations from a bank available before the query.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Sparse keys reproduce popularity or stale session context.
hypotheses.next_gate: Same last-bucket/different prior-prefix worlds, unavailable suffix, mature bank/build clock and distinct-user support.
hypotheses.testable_prediction: Matching last buckets but different earlier prefixes can retrieve different mature continuations; unavailable suffixes must never affect output.
hypotheses.nearest_experiment: Literal same-last-bucket/different-prefix and unavailable-suffix cases, followed by a frozen maturity/build/support contract.
hypotheses.benefit_towardTask1: Tests reusable automatically composed history matching for candidate coverage while preserving fullY and temporal availability.

hypotheses.mechanism: Retrieve an item supported by exact joint occurrence of two query seeds, keeping pairwise projections as matched controls.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Supported joint patterns are too rare and partial matches/popularity are better.
hypotheses.next_gate: Eight-triple equal-pair worlds, peer/duplicate invariance, charged mining/support and actual-C controls.
hypotheses.testable_prediction: Equal pairwise projections can hide different triples and produce different joint-completion candidates; sparse support can still defeat the mechanism.
hypotheses.nearest_experiment: Eight-triple equal-pair worlds, peer/duplicate invariance and paid mining/global-state/actual-C contract before a new pilot.
hypotheses.benefit_towardTask1: Tests a compositional candidate operator with a falsifiable mechanism and coverage/size/cost controls for the automated pipeline.
